technical.lead: Cerebras CBRS prints all-time high on dual Goldman + Citi Buy initiations
technical.body: Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ: CBRS) closed Wednesday at $224.85, up 3.6 percent from Tuesday's $217.05 and lifting the stock to a fresh intraday high of $228.40 on roughly 21.4 million shares — the sixth-highest post-IPO session — after Goldman Sachs analyst Toshiya Hari initiated coverage pre-market at Buy with a $260 twelve-month target, paired with a Citi Buy initiation at $245, both citing the Saudi Aramco Digital MoU close as resolving the S-1 customer-concentration overhang. The Cboe September 2026 $240 call line crossed 92,400 open contracts (first six-figure-equivalent strike build since the post-Alphabet analyst-day Friday), implied 30-day realized-vol band compressed to 58 percent from 71 percent, and institutional buyside net position lifted to approximately 49.8 percent of float from 47.5 percent on Tuesday.

technical.lead: Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 CVE-2026-46198 lands on CISA KEV inside 24 hours
technical.body: Anthropic published a Wednesday advisory disclosing CVE-2026-46198, a CVSS 8.7 prompt-injection-escalation variant in the Claude Code 3.0 MCP-server tool-call deserialization path on dev branch v3.0.14-rc2 — the same JSON-Schema validation gap class that Trail of Bits Vasilios Mavroudis and Pillar Security Dor Sarig surfaced in the OpenAI Codex CLI on Tuesday. Anthropic shipped a patched v3.0.14 stable tag with strict schema validation plus a runtime tool-call audit-log primitive and committed to a 48-hour force-roll for v3.0.13-and-earlier tenants. CISA placed the CVE on KEV Wednesday afternoon after Mandiant confirmed a second Fortune 500 incident-response engagement (this time at a healthcare customer), and Sysdig clocked the median credential-extraction time-to-first-exploit on unprotected v3.0.13 estates at 3 minutes 40 seconds, down from the Codex CLI baseline of 5 minutes — taking the Trail of Bits agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE taxonomy to thirteen catalogued instances.

technical.lead: vLLM v0.11.5-rc1 ships Qwen3.6-Max MoE expert-fused router at 22,140 tok/s
technical.body: The vLLM project cut its v0.11.5 development branch to release-candidate tag v0.11.5-rc1 on Wednesday afternoon Pacific time, the first development-branch RC since v0.11.4 stable (May 18) and the first vLLM RC to ship native Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B Mixture-of-Experts kernel support with the expert-fused-router pass that Tianle Cai and Woosuk Kwon prototyped in the May 12 project-meeting notes. The RC measures 22,140 tokens per second on the Yotta Labs canonical 8x H200 SXM5 + 1500-concurrent benchmark (14.4 percent over v0.11.4 stable's 19,355 baseline), drops Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B FP8 first-token-latency median to 0.142 seconds from 0.181 seconds, and lifts prefill cache hit-rate to 79.4 percent from 71.3 percent on the radix-prefix-tree-v2 path; Together AI and Fireworks AI rotated 38 percent of their Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B serving footprint to the RC inside six hours, and SGLang RadixArk v0.5.9 maintainer Lianmin Zheng confirmed parity tracking inside a 1.0 percent throughput gap.

technical.lead: Stanford + DeepMind ship Reservoir Routing primitive — 4.1pp SWE-Bench uplift
technical.body: A fresh ArXiv submission by Stanford CRFM PhD candidate Aryaman Arora and DeepMind senior research scientist Aakanksha Chowdhery dropped Wednesday morning Pacific at arxiv.org/abs/2605.10142 — 'Reservoir Routing: A Stateful Mixture-of-Experts Path for Long-Horizon Agentic Inference' — proposing a router-state-bank primitive that caches expert-selection trajectories across multi-turn agentic conversations rather than recomputing routing at every token. On a 145B-parameter MoE backbone (Qwen3 MoE 60B uplifted with the Tsinghua KEG Lab MiniMax M2.7 235B port from Unsloth v2026.5.26), reservoir routing recovers 4.1 percentage points of SWE-Bench Verified — landing the augmented backbone at 78.7 against the published 74.6 baseline on tool-use chains exceeding eight tool calls — while cutting per-turn router-compute cost by 31.4 percent on an 8x H100 SXM5 reference node. Simon Willison flagged the paper as the first credible reservoir-style routing primitive on a contemporary frontier-class MoE backbone, and Hacker News surfaced two early Lambda Labs reproductions inside a 2.5 percent throughput envelope.

technical.lead: Apollo Gen 2 ten-unit cohort live at Mercedes-Benz Tuscaloosa assembly
technical.body: Apptronik announced Wednesday morning that its Apollo Generation 2 humanoid platform has cleared the first ten-unit cohort deployment at Mercedes-Benz's Tuscaloosa, Alabama final-assembly plant, operating on a single-shift rotation across body-shop material-handoff and door-line subassembly stations. The ten units cleared a 120-hour continuous-operation pre-flight (Saturday through Wednesday) at the Tuscaloosa fixture with zero MTBF events before Wednesday day-shift release, and Mercedes-Benz confirmed an additional 14-unit second cohort already wheeled into the commissioning bay for a June 10 first-activation target. The deployment compresses the prior April 22 Mercedes-Apptronik MoU's nine-month single-digit-cohort ramp curve into a six-week first-deployment window and lifts the humanoid-on-factory-floor OEM-platform pair count to seven (Tesla-Fremont, Stellantis-Detroit, BMW-Leipzig, BMW-Spartanburg, Volkswagen-Wolfsburg, Boston Dynamics Hyundai-Pyeongtaek, Apptronik-Mercedes-Tuscaloosa); Wall Street's Wednesday afternoon reaction lifted humanoid-pure-play valuation comps (Figure, Sanctuary AI, Unitree H1 private secondaries) by a weighted 4.7 percent.
